condition: pediatric molluscum contagiosum clusters of tiny pearly dimpled trunk bumps
level_rationale: Six weeks of 12 tiny pearly dimpled bumps on a 5-year-old girl's right side with the surrounding skin turning red and itchy this week indicates symptomatic pediatric papular dermatosis with perilesional eczematous inflammation warranting a routine outpatient physician visit for diagnostic confirmation and safe topical management rather than emergency care, whereas large sheets of tender red skin peeling off around those bumps today signals acute exfoliative toxin-mediated skin sloughing requiring immediate ER fluid resuscitation and parenteral antimicrobial therapy.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + single-fact same-site pediatric skin exfoliation escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4).

design_note: Three atomic positive reference facts cover a 5-year-old daughter, 6 weeks of 12 tiny pearly dimpled bumps on her right side, and surrounding skin turning red and itchy this week without naming molluscum contagiosum, with a 2-word span difference (16 vs 18 words) and identical digit multisets across all 5 variants. Overriding plan.json's multi-symptom nonblanching-spots-plus-fever hint under Rules A and D, replacing f3 at the exact same right-side bump site with acute sheet-like skin peeling ('and large sheets of tender red skin started peeling off around those bumps today', suspected staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome complicating pediatric trunk papules) adds zero new body sites or stated negatives and escalates care unambiguously from doctor (level 2) to ER (level 4).
